algorithm.name: Ducos optimized subresultant PRS
algorithm.reference: Lionel Ducos, J. Pure Appl. Algebra 2000; AbstractAlgebra.jl resultant_subresultant
steps: Set p0 = P, p1 = dP/du in R[u], R = Q[A,B,Y,Z]
Iterate pseudo-remainder subresultant steps until deg <= 1
Output the degree-1 (or lower) subresultant polynomial S = s1*u + s0
operations: exact division by previous lc powers (content-correct Ducos correction)

evaluation.at_point: specialize P to Q[u]; run univariate Ducos PRS; read coeff(S,1), coeff(S,0)
evaluation.mod_p: same over GF(p)[A,B,Y,Z][u]; full expansion of s0,s1 mod p is feasible but dense (intermediate Sres_2 ~3.5e5 terms mod 67)

expansion_status.reason: PRS intermediate deg-2 poly has ~3.5e5 multipoly terms mod p; exact QQ expansion exceeds exploratory densification budget
expansion_status.accepted_by_workorder: exact sparse polynomials OR exact straight-line circuits

principal_subresultant_coefficients.PSC_0: Res_u(P, P_u) = H * G (installed as exact quotient circuit; not re-expanded)
principal_subresultant_coefficients.PSC_1: leading coefficient of Sres_1 when deg Sres_1 = 1; equals s_1 under that degree hypothesis
principal_subresultant_coefficients.PSC_k_k_ge_2: control deg gcd >= 2; vanish of PSC_1 (with Res=0) is the deg-gcd >= 2 locus

identity: Sres_1 lies in the ideal (P, P_u) as an R[u]-linear combination (Bézout/subresultant identity); on D(s1) one has u = -s0/s1 in the quotient whenever deg gcd = 1
